newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Hongkong Land sees '98 launch of Singapore project.
newsitem.headline: Hongkong Land sees '98 launch of Singapore project.

text.p: Hongkong Land said on Tuesday it expects to launch the marketing of its Singapore $600 million office project in Singapore by the middle of 1998.

Executive director Ian Hawksworth told reporters after the ground breaking ceremony for the project that marketing of the building would be targetted mainly at the investment banking and financial sector.
He declined to give revenue projections for the building but said rents were likely to be "above the current market rates".
Property analysts said office rents in Marina Centre, where the new Hongkong Land building is being built, are around Singapore S$71 psm.

Hongkong Land's new six storey building will have total of 25,175 sq m of office space and 11,555 sm of retail space, half of it inside a subterranean mall linking the building to the Raffles City MRT interchange.

Speaking on soft office rents in Singapore, Hawsworth said: "The market for commercial space has plateaued with a great deal of supply coming on in 1997 and into 1998 due to higher completions (of buildings)."
He said there was a window of limited supply by mid-1999 to 2000 and that was when the group has timed the completion of its building.
Hawksworth said the payback period for project "will be longish" as the Singapore property market was quite mature and yields fairly low.

He also said Hongkong Land would continue to look for investment opportunities in other Asian capitals with the focus would be on prime office space for investment and the luxury end of the residential market for trading.
Recently, the group participated in the tender of a prime residential site in Singapore.
Hawksworth said the group would continue to have a leading pressence in Hong Kong, especially in prime commercial space in the central business district.

He said redevelopment plans for a 650,000 sq ft office tower on the site of Swire House had been submitted to the government for approval and the proposal would be presented to the board before the end of the year.
Hawksworth said the group's exercise to renew existing commercial leases in Hong Kong had been "positive", though prices achieved are off the 1994 peak.
"In the last 12 months, prices have been stabilising and we have seen an increase in demand which is putting some pressure on prices," he said.
